verdicts.strongest_argument: Every input is in a press release. Q1 FY27 revenue $220.23m and the Q2 guide of $219-221m/28% are in the 2026-06-10 release; Q1 FY26 $157.5m is the stated comparative in that same release; Q3 FY26 $195m and 9M FY26 $524m are in the 2025-12-15 release, so Q2 FY26 of ~$171.5m is a single subtraction from two wire-distributed documents (the hunter's $172.2m and +9.6% are slightly off; true is $171.5m and +8.9%). More damaging, management pre-empted the inference on the Q1 call: Navan guided to a 'seasonally slightly weaker summer season', a phrase that was carried into the wire summaries of the guide (MarketScreener, 2026-06-10). So the street has not 'failed to apply seasonality' — it applied the seasonality management supplied. And the conclusion the finding is really making, that the guide is sandbagged and Navan beats, is the explicitly published sell-side call: Oppenheimer on 2026-08-27 named the very consensus figures ($220.5m revenue, $2.86bn bookings) and said it expects Navan to exceed both, lifting its target to $35; BofA went to $34 from $26 in early September. The market has also watched this company beat its own guide midpoint by ~10% ($161-163m guided, $178m printed for Q4 FY26) and gap +43%, then beat and raise and gap +8.4%. A serial sandbagger sandbagging is structural, not news. What is left unpriced is only the specific quantified sequential comparison — nobody I found has written 'flat vs +9% last year' — which is worth something but not much against 110% ATM IV and a 14% implied move.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Q1 FY27 revenue $220m (+40%), Q1 FY26 comparative $157.5m, Q2 FY27 guide $219-221m at 28% growth, FY27 raised to $907-913m.
Wire summary of the Q2 guide, carrying management's framing that the $219-221m/28% covers 'a seasonally slightly weaker summer season'.
Q3 FY26 revenue $195m and nine-month FY26 revenue $524m — the two numbers from which Q2 FY26 is subtracted.
Oppenheimer raises target to $35 from $30 and says it expects Navan to exceed consensus bookings of $2.86bn and revenue of $220.5m for Q2 FY27.
Q4 FY26 revenue $178m against a guide of $161-163m — the ~10% guide-beat pattern the market has already seen and paid for.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Reaction history is two large upside gaps on beats (+43.28% on 2026-03-25, +8.43% on 2026-06-10) against one -11.86%; the beat-and-gap pattern is exactly what a 110.9% ATM IV and a 14.06% event-implied move are charging for. Put/call open interest of 0.26 says the surviving open interest is overwhelmingly calls, i.e. the upside case is the one being bought, not the neglected one.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A published sell-side or press note showing consensus sits meaningfully above the guide midpoint, or evidence that FY26's Q1-to-Q2 sequential step was driven by something that cannot recur, would move this either way.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This is h1#0 arrived at independently, and it rests on the single most-read document in the name — the 2026-06-10 release — which is also the document that contains the rebuttal. Management characterised Q2 on that call as 'a seasonally slightly weaker summer season' and quantified the price channel at only 3pp of the 50pp Q1 gross-bookings growth, assuming 'prices being fairly stable in Q2'. The $240m extrapolation is the weakest part: it assumes FY26 seasonality repeats unchanged on a base 40% larger, with a different revenue mix (payments and subscription now growing at different rates) and a Brazilian acquisition folded in, and it sits awkwardly against a full-year guide of $907-913m that the company had just raised. As magnitude it is contested rather than established. And the trade it implies — Navan beats its guide by ~9% — is the published Oppenheimer (2026-08-27, $35 target) and BofA (early September, $34 from $26) call, on a stock the market has already watched beat its own Q4 guide by 9.9% and gap +43%.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Contains both halves of the arithmetic — Q1 FY27 $220.23m and Q1 FY26 $157.5m — plus the Q2 guide of $219-221m.
Management calls Q2 a 'seasonally slightly weaker summer season' and attributes only 3pp of Q1's 50% bookings growth to travel inflation, assuming stable prices in Q2.
Publicly calls for a beat on the exact consensus revenue figure ($220.5m) this finding says is unchallenged.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Two of three prior prints were upside gaps on beats, median absolute move 11.86%, event-implied move 14.06% — the option market is already paying full price for a large surprise in either direction. Nothing in the 20-day run-up (-7.19%) is explained by fundamental news; two brokers raised targets into that decline.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence that consensus for Q2 sits at or above ~$232m — i.e. that the street has in fact modelled last year's sequential — would flip this to near-zero, since the finding would then be arguing something already in the numbers.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The macro input is about as public as a number can be: BLS CPI is a scheduled monthly release with universal wire coverage, the July print landed on 2026-08-12 with airline fares +25.5% y/y called out, and dedicated trackers (usinflationcalculator's airfare page, NerdWallet's monthly travel inflation report) publish the series continuously. It is also already connected to Navan in print — Navan itself published its Business Travel Benchmark on 2026-07-14, covered by Business Travel News, BTN Europe and TravelMole, showing H1 2026 platform fares up 14.4% domestic and 9.1% international with spend +21.5% on 8.8% higher volume. That is Navan's own realised fare inflation and it is roughly half the CPI print, which is the honest rebuttal to the magnitude: leisure-weighted, US-only, hedonically adjusted CPI is not the pass-through Navan books. Management put a number on the channel — 3pp of 50pp of Q1 bookings growth from travel inflation — so a 12pp CPI step-up is worth low single digits of bookings growth, not 12. Oppenheimer's 2026-08-27 note explicitly cites 'a solid corporate travel environment' and supportive travel-supplier earnings as its reason to expect a bookings beat against the very $2.86bn the finding calls unchallenged. What survives: the specific observation that $2.86bn is a -7.7% sequential against +1% in the same fiscal quarters last year is arithmetic I could not find published anywhere, and it does check out against the disclosed FY26 GBV of $9.1bn.

prior_publication.what_it_says: July 2026 CPI: airline fares +25.5% year over year, released on the standard schedule with full wire coverage.
Navan's own H1 2026 platform data: domestic fares +14.4%, international +9.1%, spend +21.5% on 8.8% more volume — a materially lower fare-inflation read than CPI, published by the company itself.
Publishes the $2.86bn bookings consensus and says Oppenheimer expects Navan to exceed it, citing supportive travel-supplier earnings and a solid corporate travel backdrop.
Trade-press coverage tying Navan's index to H1 2026 business-travel and fare growth.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The May-July CPI prints landed on 2026-06-10, 07-14 and 08-12; the stock rose through all of them to an all-time high close of $30.58 on 08-27, so the tailwind was being paid for, not ignored. The subsequent -12.2% from that high is not attributable to any fare data. Call-dominated open interest (put/call 0.26) is consistent with the upside backdrop already being the popular side.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A disclosure or credible check that Navan's air take is ad-valorem rather than largely per-transaction, which would make CPI pass-through much closer to one-for-one and make the magnitude real rather than contested.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Structurally the same claim as h1#1 with better index construction (the seasonally-adjusted 291.3 to 310.0 sequential move is a nicer statistic than the y/y pairs, and I found it published nowhere), but with no company-specific arithmetic at all — it is a wire-level macro series set against a wire-level guidance number. Both halves are fully published: the BLS release of 2026-08-12 and the $219-221m/28% guide of 2026-06-10. The bridging mechanism is where it fails to reach: management already told the market on that same call that travel inflation contributed 3pp of 50pp of bookings growth and that it assumed 'prices being fairly stable in Q2', and Navan's own July benchmark put its platform fare inflation at 9-14%, not 26%. So the '12pp step-up in the dollar-price tailwind' does not convert into anything like 12pp of revenue. The deceleration from 40% to 28% that the finding treats as unexplained is also the least surprising number in the release — it is what the company guided, what the wires reported, and what an analyst asked about on the call, where the CFO answered it directly.

prior_publication.what_it_says: July 2026 CPI, airline fares +25.5% y/y — the scheduled public release this claim is built on.
Maintains a running public series of airline-ticket CPI inflation through 2026, so the acceleration is tracked continuously outside BLS itself.
CFO quantifies travel inflation at 3pp of Q1's 50% bookings growth and assumes stable Q2 prices; the 40%-to-28% deceleration is asked and answered on the call.
Monthly consumer-facing travel inflation report tracking the same fare series.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Same as h1#1 — the stock made its all-time high on 2026-08-27, fifteen days after the July CPI print, so the fare acceleration coincided with strength rather than being missed. Nothing in the run-up or skew marks the fare data as a surprise still to come.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence that Navan's air mix is skewed to the US domestic routes where CPI ran hottest, and that its revenue on air scales with ticket price rather than transaction count.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This claim asks to reinterpret a price move that has already fully happened, using filings that are already published and syndicated. The Form 4s are on EDGAR and are picked up by StockTitan's NAVN filings feed and Investing.com's insider-trading desk, which has covered Cohen's sales before; the 10b5-1 plan adopted 2026-01-06 is disclosed in Navan's own periodic Rule 408 disclosure, including its 225,000-share Class A cap — which is exactly the 3 x 75,000 the trusts sold, i.e. the plan simply ran out. The drawdown itself is in the sealed baseline (run_up_20d -7.19%, -12.2% from the 52-week high) and is therefore in the price by construction. The causal mechanism is the weak part and I think it is wrong: 393,378 shares is roughly $11.9m against 20-day average volume of 2.16m shares, about 18% of one session, and it printed on 2026-08-27 — the day of the $30.58 all-time high close, not during the decline that followed. A far better-supported account of that day is Oppenheimer's target raise to $35, published the same day, producing a spike and fade, followed by de-risking into a print carrying a 14% implied move on a stock ten months from IPO. Calling a nine-session, twelve-percent drawdown 'mechanical' on the basis of a completed one-day sale is not a mechanism that reaches.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Cohen's 2026-08-27 open-market sale of 168,378 shares at $30.1441 under the Rule 10b5-1 plan, plus 75,000 from each of the Lihi, Shai and Sivan Cohen GST Trusts.
StockTitan indexes and narrates NAVN Form 4 insider activity as it is filed, so these filings surface outside EDGAR within a day.
Investing.com runs a dedicated news item on each Cohen Form 4, establishing that these filings get wire-adjacent coverage.
All-time-high close of $30.58 on 2026-08-27 and $28.50 on 08-28 — the drawdown began the session after the sale was complete.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The baseline already carries the entire move this finding is trying to explain: pct_from_52w_high -12.2%, run_up_20d_pct -7.19%. Whatever caused it is in the spot. Meanwhile two brokers raised targets into that decline (Oppenheimer to $35 on 08-27, BofA to $34 from $26 in early September), so the tape is not carrying a fundamental de-rating either — but that is an argument the price has already made without this finding.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Volume-by-day evidence showing the sale actually cleared over the 08-28 to 09-08 window rather than in one session on 08-27, plus a size that is material against $60m a day of turnover.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The same accession as h1#2, read the opposite way, and the reading does not survive the filing itself. The sale was executed under a Rule 10b5-1 plan adopted on 2026-01-06 — eight months before the print and disclosed in Navan's periodic Rule 408 disclosure — which caps Class A sales at 225,000 shares, precisely the 3 x 75,000 the trusts sold. 'All three trusts went to zero' is the plan finishing on schedule, not a decision taken nine sessions before earnings, and h1#2 correctly records the plan date while this finding omits it, which is the omission that produces the bearish reading. The Lightspeed distributions of June 2026 at $19-20 are likewise routine post-IPO LP distributions, filed on Form 4 on 2026-06-23 and indexed by the same aggregators; the stock is $26.85 today, 35% above where they distributed, which is a poor advertisement for treating it as a signal. And the whole category — sponsor distribution and founder sales in a company ten months from its IPO — is the definition of structural and known. Two brokers raised targets into the same window (Oppenheimer $35 on 08-27, BofA $34 in early September); the sell-side saw the same filings and did not read them as a warning.

prior_publication.what_it_says: The 08-27 sales, with the footnote that they were made under a Rule 10b5-1 plan adopted 2026-01-06.
Lightspeed-entity Form 4 covering the June distribution the finding describes — filed and public two and a half months before the print.
Navan proxy/periodic disclosure of the Cohen Rule 10b5-1 arrangement adopted 2026-01-06, expiring 2026-10-31, covering up to 225,000 Class A shares plus 433,098 RSU-settled shares.
NAVN filings and news feed carries the Form 4s as they post.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The 25-delta skew of +5.64 vol points is the only baseline datum pointing this way, and the baseline's own warning caps what it can bear: the ATM bid-ask is 43% of mid on 3,367 total contracts, and put/call open interest is 0.26 — four calls open for every put. That is not a book paying for downside protection; it is a thin book where the skew number is noise. The -7.19% 20-day run-up already absorbed whatever supply there was.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A discretionary, non-10b5-1 sale by an executive with access to the quarter, or an amendment or early termination of the January plan, either of which would restore the signal content this finding assumes.

interactions: Three pairs, each independently derived, and each pair should count once rather than twice. (1) NAVN-h1#0 and NAVN-h2#1 are the same arithmetic on the same two press releases — h1 routes it through the 2025-12-15 Q3 FY26 release and gets Q1 FY26 $157.1m to Q2 FY26 $172.2m (+9.6%); h2 routes it through the 2026-06-10 Q1 FY27 release and gets $157.5m to $171.9m (+9.1%). Against the filings the true figures are $157.5m and $171.5m, +8.9%. The convergence is genuine and slightly raises my confidence that the observation is correct, but it is one fact, and both are answered by the same sentence in the same transcript ('seasonally slightly weaker summer season') and by the same Oppenheimer note. (2) NAVN-h1#1 and NAVN-h2#0 are the same BLS release of 2026-08-12 and the same ~12pp step-up, with h1 adding the consensus-GBV sequential and h2 adding the seasonally-adjusted index levels. One macro fact, two dressings; both are cut by the same two documents — Navan's own 2026-07-14 benchmark showing platform fare inflation of 9-14% rather than 26%, and the CFO's 3pp-of-50pp quantification. (3) NAVN-h1#2 and NAVN-h2#2 rest on the identical EDGAR accession 000185373026000011 and reach opposite conclusions from it: h1 reads the 08-27 sale as benign mechanical supply that explains away the drawdown (bullish for the setup), h2 reads the same sale as a bearish pre-print signal. They cannot both be scored, and h1 has the better of it because it records the 2026-01-06 10b5-1 plan date that h2 omits — the omission is what generates h2's direction. Netted, the Form 4 carries approximately zero directional content and should not contribute on either side. Separately, note that the consensus anchors both hunters lean on ($220.5m revenue, $2.86bn bookings) come from the same Oppenheimer note of 2026-08-27 that also publishes an explicit call for Navan to beat both — the hunters' evidence and its refutation are the same document.
